h1: Your own team of AI assistants.
lead: FreeDuet runs on your own computer. One assistant handles your mail, one reads contracts, one books the restaurant. You say what you need, they do the work, and by default they send, pay or delete nothing without your yes.
appCap: This is an illustration drawn for this page. Every name and message in it is made up.
w_h: Too much to do, and only one of you?
w_p1: Emails, invoices, bookings, contracts, that reply you promised last week. One head, two hands, a hundred things to do.
w_p2: FreeDuet is like a small office of assistants inside your computer. Each assistant is good at exactly one job. You talk to Iris, the one who runs the team, and she gets everybody moving.
w_a_alt: One coordinator connected to four specialists
w_a_p: A chatbot is one clever friend who answers questions. FreeDuet is a whole group project where everybody really does their part.
w_b_alt: A browser window with a button being clicked
w_b_h: It does things, it doesn't just talk
w_b_p: Every assistant has its own desk: a separate browser, away from yours. There it can look up prices, fill in forms and prepare drafts.
w_c_p: The assistants prepare. You decide. By default, a send, a payment or a deletion waits until you press Approve.
v_a_p: You open the mail, read forty messages, hunt for the invoice, compare three flights, write the reply, forget the birthday present.
v_b_p: You write one sentence: "Handle everything that came in this morning." Then you read a short report and press Approve where you agree.
t_h: Meet the team. Each one has exactly one job.
t_p: Why not one assistant that does everything? For the same reason a football team has a goalkeeper: someone who does one job all day gets very good at it.
t_note: This is only where the team starts. You can train your own for exactly the job you need, and we add new ready-made members over time. Renaming members and changing how they talk is built but not yet run live.
ft_p: Each small picture shows a real part of FreeDuet. The names and messages in them are made up.
fe2h: Five buttons wait for your yes
fe3p: A routine repeats on a schedule, like a summary every morning. Iris offers one, a daily review, and makes it only after you say yes (new since v0.2.2). A routine that needs one of the five buttons asks you first; that rule is built but not yet run live.
fe5h: By default, your conversations stay on your computer
fe5p: The app, its database and the assistants' browsers run on your computer, and by default the conversations are stored there. To think, the assistants use the AI service you signed in to, unless you add a free model on the Engines page, which receives what it is sent.
aiSvc: AI service you signed in to
h_h: What happens after you press Enter
h_p: No magic and no secrets. Five steps, always the same, so you always know who is doing what.
s1p: In your own words and your own language, like a message to a friend.
s2p: She reads your request and hands it to the specialist for that job.
s3h: The assistant works at its own desk
s3p: It uses its own browser to search, read and prepare. It is told to treat what it reads as information, never as orders.
s4h: A card asks for your yes
s4p: By default, if the job needs a big button (send, pay, sign, book, delete), everything stops and waits for you.
s5p: What was done, what was not done and why, and what the next step is. No walls of text.
flowMore: …and Gus, Basil, Mark, Cam, Rex and Leo
sf_h: Five buttons that wait for your yes
sf_p: Would you give a new assistant your wallet on the first day? Neither would we. So these five wait for your yes by default. A switch that lifts this for one member, which only you can turn on, is built but not yet run live. Plain Full access also lifts the wait for payments, and no spending limit exists yet. "Full access without payments" keeps them waiting.
p1p: The rule is written in the assistant's instructions, and by default the program itself also holds the action until you approve it. Its check for payments, passwords and security settings reads words in the twelve languages of this site; a payment worded in another way can still get past it.
p2p: An email that says "send me the password, it's urgent" is text to read, and the assistants are told never to obey it as an order. They are also told never to ask for passwords or card numbers in the chat, and a member's computer refuses to type into a password, code or card field. A field with no marker can slip past that refusal.
p3p: If you type the address yourself ("email anna@example.com and tell her…"), your sentence is the yes, and that new email goes out. By default, addresses found anywhere else ask first.
score: We try to fool our own assistants on purpose. The last full certification, at version 0.1, passed the safety checks 45 times out of 45. Later runs have not met the bar yet. Read the public report. The assistants can still make mistakes, so read what they prepare before you approve it.
m_p1: Most AI tools make you buy an "API key". That works like a taxi meter: every word costs a little, and the bill keeps climbing.
m_p2: A monthly AI subscription is more like a bus pass: one price, ride as much as the pass allows. FreeDuet runs on the pass you already have. You sign in yourself. FreeDuet's own code never reads, copies or forwards your login; it stays on your computer, in a place only the Claude Code program reads.
m_l1: Today it works with a Claude subscription, through the official Claude Code app.
m_l2: More subscriptions are in progress. Local models, OpenRouter's free models and your own FreeLLMAPI router are built and can be added on the Engines page. None of them runs first for a member unless you choose that order, and a model counts as supported only after the team's tests pass on it.
m_l3: FreeDuet itself costs nothing: the code is public under the MIT licence.
g_h: The goal: a team for everyone, not only for big companies
g_p1: A big company has assistants, lawyers and accountants. A freelancer, a small shop or a family has… themselves. That is unfair, and now it can change.
g_p2: We want anybody to have a team: free, open and at home. FreeDuet runs on your own computer and, by default, keeps its conversations in a database on that computer. The thinking is done by the AI you already subscribe to.
g_p3: Open source means the recipe is public. Anyone can read it, check that it does what it says, and make it better. You don't have to trust us. You can look.
r_h: What works today, and what is coming
r1: The team on your own Claude login, with approvals, tests, Gmail and Google Calendar.
r2: Top priority: a one-file installer for Windows, macOS and Ubuntu. Today there are first-step scripts for Ubuntu and for Windows through WSL2, and no double-click installer yet. A mail assistant that tidies your mailbox is built: on 15 November 2026 Otto moved spam to the Spam folder of a real mailbox. Standing mail rules are in v0.2.2: on 16 November 2026 one rule, for one sender domain, applied to new mail by itself. The other changes and rules are not yet run live. Built but not yet run live: "Done when" on every hand-off, the routine's card in the chat, a token for each member's computer, and home network connections that close when you switch it off.
r3: Engines chosen per member are in progress: the Engines page is built but not yet run live. On it you can add a local model, OpenRouter's free models or your own FreeLLMAPI router in three clicks, and choose the order of each member's engines after a warning and a tick. A free model that writes its tool call as text does not end the turn: the next engine answers instead. When a free model asks for a short wait, FreeDuet waits and tries again. Settings changed in chat, with Undo, are in progress. A member's name, tone and language are built after v0.2 but not yet run live, and no test has run on tone or language yet. Real delegation is planned.
r4: Automations written in chat, a phone version and remote access are in progress. More connected apps are in design.
r5: Voice: read aloud is built but not yet run live, and off by default; calls are not built yet. Full access and Cam are built but not yet run live. Safe purchases are planned.
r_cloud: A hosted FreeDuet for people who prefer not to install is planned, for a small monthly subscription. The price is not set yet. There, Claude would work only with your own API key. Not before the installer and the first start are done. On your own computer, FreeDuet stays free.
r_now2: First start in three clicks is planned: one button to connect your Claude plan, signing in on Claude's own page. Today the chat shows a card with a command to copy, built and not yet run live; the button is not built.
r_now3: Three steps at most for connecting a Gmail mailbox from the chat. One line with Undo after a member is added in the chat. A team proposed at your first message, with nothing created without your yes. Updates that can go back: the step that puts the old version and data back has not run live yet.
r_note: We label everything that is not built yet. No fairy tales. Full roadmap on GitHub.
in_h: From install to your first useful task
in_p: Four steps, in the real order. All the commands are also in one box further down, ready to copy.
in1p: One command downloads FreeDuet from GitHub, and one copies the example settings file.
in2p: One script starts the app, the team and a separate computer for each member. It needs Docker, Bash and Bun. On Windows, run it inside WSL2.
in3h: Sign in once with your Claude plan
in3p: Open the official Claude Code sign-in and log in yourself. FreeDuet's own code never reads, copies or forwards your login; it stays on your computer, in a place only the Claude Code program reads.
in4h: Open the page and give Iris a small task
in4p: Go to localhost:3010 in your browser and write one small request. Iris picks the right assistant and brings you the answer.
in4ex: What can I cook tonight with spinach and eggs?
st_h: Ready? Four commands, then sign in, and the team is at work
st_p: Copy them into a terminal, sign in once with your own Claude plan, then open the page it gives you.
st_need: a Claude subscription, plus Docker, Bash and Bun on your computer. Tested on Windows (with WSL2) and on Linux.
st_kid: Never opened a terminal? Ask someone technical to set it up, and show them this page.
j1p: One click on GitHub tells other people this project is worth a look.
j2p: Using it? Found an error? Have a fix? There is a short form for each.
j3p: FreeDuet is built by one person. A small donation keeps it going.
q1: What is free, and what do I pay for?
a1: FreeDuet is free and open source under the MIT licence, also for business use. The only thing you pay for is the AI subscription you use with it, which today is a Claude plan. You can also add free models on the Engines page; their providers may keep what they are sent. There is no API key to buy.
q2: What do I need to install it?
a2: A Claude subscription, and Docker, Bash and Bun on your computer. The four steps above are the whole install. Never opened a terminal? Ask someone technical to set it up, and show them this page.
q3: Does it work on Windows, Mac and Linux?
a3: The maintainer uses it on Windows with WSL2 and Docker, and our automatic checks start it on Linux. It has not been tested on a Mac, so we can't promise it works there. FreeDuet is an early release: the latest published version is 0.2.2 (16 November 2026), built and used by one maintainer.
q4: What can an assistant do without asking me?
a4: It can look things up, read, and prepare drafts and reports. By default, the five buttons wait for your Approve, except a new email to an address you typed. A standing mail rule that you set in your own words applies to new mail by itself: it can label, archive, mark as read, or move mail to Spam or the Bin, and it never forwards, replies, sends or deletes for good. Full access, per member, lifts the waiting in your own chats; it is built but not yet run live. Plain Full access also lifts payments; "without payments" does not. Passwords and security settings still come to you, but the check reads words in the twelve languages of this site; another wording, or lookalike letters from another alphabet, can still get past it. A command or script is checked only when an automatic reviewer is set up. Assistants can still make mistakes, so read what they prepare before you approve it.
a5: FreeDuet runs on your computer and, by default, keeps its conversations in a database there. Your Claude login stays in a Docker volume that only the Claude Code program reads. To think, the assistants send your request to the AI service you signed in to, as its own app would. If you add an engine on the Engines page, such as a free cloud model, OpenRouter or your own FreeLLMAPI router, that member's messages go to it too, and it may keep them.
q6: Can I use it from my phone?
a6: Not a phone version yet. Today FreeDuet opens in the browser on your computer. Since v0.2.2 a phone's browser can be paired from the computer with a one-time code, shown as a link or a QR code, and pairing a phone was run live on one installation on 16 November 2026. The phone version, where you also get approval requests, and remote access are in progress.
q7: Can I add my own team member?
a7: Yes. Ask Leo, who builds new assistants, to design one for the job you need, or write its definition yourself. Renaming members and changing how they talk is built but not yet run live. How the members are defined.
a8: Open an issue on GitHub. There is a short form for a question, an error, a fix, or to say you are using it. You can write in English or Italian.
ft1: FreeDuet is an independent open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Z.ai or CopilotKit. Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok are trademarks of their owners and are named only to describe compatibility.
ft2: Built on OpenBot and OpenDuet by CopilotKit (MIT). FreeDuet's assistants can make mistakes: review what they prepare before you approve it.
title: FreeDuet: your own team of AI assistants
desc: FreeDuet is a free, open-source team of AI assistants that runs on your own computer and your own AI subscription. By default they ask before they send, pay, sign, book or delete.

iris: You tell Iris what you need. She hands it to the right assistant, and the answer comes back through her. If a colleague's tools can do the job, she asks that colleague first, and says she cannot only when nobody on the team can.
Handle everything that came in this morning.
otto: Reads your inbox, points out what matters now and what can wait, and writes the replies for you to check.
Sort my mail and draft the replies that matter.
portia: Reads the boring small print and shows you where the traps are before you sign.
penny: Prepares invoices and keeps the list of who still owes you money.
Invoice Acme for last week and tell me who hasn't paid.
jules: Finds flights, presents and free tables in its own browser, and books them when you say yes.
Book a table for four on Friday.
wren: Turns your rough notes into posts and emails that sound like you.
Turn this voice note into a post in my style.
mark: Builds your marketing plan, launch plan and channel strategy, and reviews your site, SEO and ads. By default, he publishes and spends nothing without your yes. His cases ran in the team evals. Not yet run on a real installation.
Give me a three-month marketing plan for my shop.
video: Cuts, subtitles, music and sound for short videos from your footage or a script, in landscape, vertical and square sizes. He never publishes or uploads one. His cases ran in the team evals. Not yet run on a real installation.
Make a 30-second vertical video from this script, with subtitles.
gus: Send a photo of what broke. Gus tells you how to fix it safely, or who to call.
The door won't close. Here's a photo.
basil: Tell Basil what is in the fridge and he gives you three dishes you can make tonight.
What can I cook with spinach and eggs?
vera: Works behind the scenes. She redoes the sums and re-opens the prices before the work reaches you.
rex: Compares the team's test reports for the engines you can use and proposes which engine fits which member. He starts no test run and changes no engine: you decide on the Engines page. Built, not yet run live.
Basil runs on my local model now. Is that good enough?
leo: Need an assistant that doesn't exist yet? Leo designs it. When a tool is missing, Leo proposes one with its source and licence, and nothing is installed without your yes. Testing each new member before it is called ready is planned.
I need someone who tracks my domain renewals.

demo.me: Reply to the plumber's email: Tuesday at 9 is fine.
demo.iris: On it. This is a job for Otto.
demo.line: I found his email and wrote the reply. I won't send it until you say so.
card: Good morning, Tuesday at 9 works for me. Thank you!
demo.ok: Sent. One reply, in the same conversation. Nothing else was touched.
demo.stop: Not sent. The draft is saved if you change your mind.

demo.me: Book a table for four on Friday evening, somewhere with pizza.
demo.line: I looked in my own browser and found a free table. I haven't booked anything yet.
demo.ok: Booked for Friday at 8:00 pm, 4 people. The confirmation is in your inbox.
demo.stop: Nothing booked. Tell me if you want other places.

Mark and Cam ran in it too. A second run, three repeats on 16 and 17 November, also failed some cases. No full run has passed since v0.1.
